videos.script: Zero-shot means asking for a task with no worked examples. Just the instruction, and the input. {{zero}} It is how most people use a chat window, and most of the time it works. {{works}} When it does not, the cause is usually in the prompt, not the model. {{cause}} The task was vague. The input ran into the instruction. Nobody said what the answer should look like. {{vague}} The odd cases were never mentioned, so the model guessed. {{edge}} In this lesson you take a weak prompt that sorts café reviews and make it strong, one fix at a time. {{fix}} Then you test both on eight messages with known labels. {{test}} The count decides whether zero-shot is enough. A feeling does not. {{count}} And when the count says no, lesson 21 adds examples. {{next}}
